    Understand and use Sworn

    Protocol behavior and local mock features are distinguished throughout. This documentation makes no wallet connections or chain requests.

    Sworn makes specific facts about Ethereum wallets readable by other applications. You can inspect a wallet, verify a historical condition, define a reusable rule, or use accepted facts to decide access. An optional NFT card displays the original wallet’s record. You do not need a card to hold or consume a fact.

    This guide describes the contract source pinned at c4ff3238390fc51962fb67e86affc20cf418126e and the revised local interface. The named deployment is Ethereum mainnet Registry 0x0da2679000ea5380d1361cc3cca7d4e8c881f766. The documentation is not a fresh deployment audit or a current wallet-state report. Published contract task.

    Start with a wallet question

    Begin with the decision you want to make: “Did this wallet participate?”, “Did it deposit during a particular window?”, or “Does it have a stored verification of this community rule?” Sworn answers defined predicates. Your application decides whether those predicates are useful for its own mint, grant, access policy or research.

    Read a wallet before paying for anything. A public address lookup does not require connecting that wallet. Look at the rule, evidence window and result state together. “No accepted fact” is different from “the historical statement is false”; an RPC failure is different again. A screenshot or green card cell is useful for navigation, but the authentic Registry’s state is the credential. Concept and integration model.

    The revised interface separates three tasks:

    TaskWhat you obtainWhat it does not do
    Mint CardOne optional transferable Sworn NFT describing its original walletIt does not start oracle verification or transfer wallet credentials to later owners
    Mint FactsAn accepted wallet fact recorded in the Registry after verification, or application of an accepted shared resultIt does not create another NFT or put a separate token inside the card
    Mint RuleAn immutable, reusable community definition with a rule IDIt does not establish that any wallet meets the rule

    “Mint Facts” is interface terminology for recording accepted facts in the contract. The card reads those facts from the Registry to render its artwork. A submitted request is not yet a minted fact. In the local mock, every transaction and result is simulated.

    Where Sworn comes from

    The initial catalog uses the WhitelistCurator onchain attention game, which ran on Ethereum mainnet in August 2026. Over 66 hours, 19,522 participating wallets left a record of timing, repeated deposits, largest sends and points. The game returned deposits in the same transaction; the persistent output was the activity record rather than retained principal. WhitelistCurator source and developer notes, catalog and historical windows.

    That record can support many different lists. A project might value early participation; another might prefer continued activity or a particular historical event. Sworn supplies named predicates and evidence records so each consumer can express its own policy. It does not declare one universal allowlist.

    Participation is not proof of a unique person. Refunded ETH can be reused, and one person can control several wallets. A fact about a largest send is not a statement of current wealth. Community Facts can also describe supported Ethereum evidence outside WhitelistCurator: belonging to the original 19,522-wallet census is not a universal Sworn requirement.

    Keep rules, facts, cards and owners separate

    A rule specifies the question: its template, contract, event or function, threshold and evidence window. A wallet fact records that the authentic Registry accepts the relevant predicate for an address. A card displays the record of the wallet that minted it. The current NFT owner may be someone else.

    The original wallet is the claimant. claimantOf(tokenId) identifies it permanently; ownerOf(tokenId) identifies whoever currently owns the collectible. Transferring a card changes the latter, not the former. The original wallet cannot mint a second card after transferring the first. Its accepted facts remain associated with it. Registry mint and ownership behavior.

    Consumers use hasTrait(wallet, id) to check a fact. They do not require tokenOf(wallet) to be nonzero. If a user supplies a card, resolve its claimant first. If an application grants access to the caller, authenticate that caller; letting someone type an arbitrary qualifying address does not prove they control it.

    The card is also not a continuously refreshed record of every direct condition. Before a wallet mints, direct facts are read from the underlying Curator getters. Mint Card saves their result, and subsequent direct checks for that original wallet use its frozen snapshot. Accepted oracle facts can still be added later. Direct snapshot and hasTrait.

    Understand the evidence classes

    The catalog has 25 built-in facts across 13 visual families. Community Facts extend the available rules through existing templates; they are not a fifth evidence class. Both chain-proven and panel-sworn routes involve agents. “Chain-proven” names the configured evidence route, not an Ethereum consensus proof of all historical computation.

    ClassExample and evidencePanel for this deployment
    Direct factsSpawned 101 reads whether the wallet joined Curator. Other direct rules cover first hour, deposit count, largest send and points.No oracle panel
    Chain-proven, walletUptime 701 counts matching historical deposit events. T1 counts events, T2 sums unsigned event values, and T4 compares a historical contract view.5 members, quorum 3
    Chain-proven, shared panelTop Weights 1201 ranks contributors by summed weightAdded, with an exact ordering and tie rule. One accepted ranking can serve multiple wallets.11 members, quorum 7
    Panel-swornPretrained 1301 checks a historical account nonce. Swarmed 601 combines seat ownership, agent bindings and accepted feedback evidence.11 members, quorum 7

    These are the source’s exact requirements: kinds 1, 2 and 4 use 5/3; kinds 3, 5 and 6 use 11/7. Generic oracle defaults do not replace them. The Registry checks the required values in the signed result. Composed templates, Registry acceptance checks.

    Swarmed is more specific than “owns an IDMD.” Its recipe reconstructs held-seat intervals, resolves agent bindings and counts accepted feedback entries during those intervals, up to the request’s pinned endpoint. It requires at least three accepted entries. The count is not necessarily three distinct jobs. A transferred-in seat does not by itself establish the fact. Exact operator question and definitions.

    Panel-sworn does not mean free-form opinion. Pretrained asks about the account nonce at a fixed block. For an EOA that is related to sent transactions; for a contract account it has different meaning, including contract creations. The predicate is the nonce returned by historical state, not a count of rows on an explorer. Sworn’s public community templates do not let you submit arbitrary prose such as “this wallet is trustworthy.” T5 and catalog-only T6.

    Mint Card: an optional record you can collect

    1. Connect the wallet whose facts the card should describe. In the local lab, use Mock wallet.
    2. Open Mint Card and inspect the direct-fact snapshot. An empty snapshot is still a snapshot.
    3. Review the fee and the approval/mint steps. A wallet signs each required transaction separately.
    4. Wait for transaction confirmation and the refreshed Registry read. Then open Wallet to inspect the card.

    The pinned contract charges 0.1 IMD plus transaction gas. It mints once per original wallet and does not invoke an oracle. Transferable ownership is a collectible feature, not transferable eligibility. If you only need a wallet predicate for an application, you can leave the card unminted. Mint implementation.

    Mint Facts: request, verify, then store

    1. Choose the fact and inspect its immutable definition, claimant and block window. Preview the complete composed question, including its definitions.
    2. Check the current oracle quote and the request’s maximum price. Payment buys an attempt, not a guaranteed accepted fact.
    3. Confirm the required approval and request transaction. A confirmed request starts asynchronous verification.
    4. Observe the panel. A member’s answer, enough agreeing answers, and a signed attestation are distinct stages.
    5. Wait for Registry acceptance and the matching wallet fact read. Only then treat the fact as stored for that wallet.

    The Composer generates the request from the rule. The Registry binds the pending request to its question hash and window, and later checks the signature’s domain, signer, panel requirements, validity and result. A valid signature alone is insufficient if it answers the wrong question. These checks bind the result; they do not independently re-execute the offchain evidence collection. Request and callback flow, official IMD oracle reference.

    Personal requests accept one fact ID per upgrade call. The same wallet cannot open another request for an already-pending or already-verified fact. A frontend can prepare a sequence of requests, but they remain separate transactions and paid attempts. Accepted oracle facts are permanent historical records, not subscriptions that keep checking present conditions. Registry request guards.

    In the revised mock, progress appears in the popup and at the top of the page. You can dismiss the page panel; it stays dismissed across navigation and reload for those requests. Review transaction steps retains the result. Closing either view does not cancel verification. New requests receive their own progress panel. All agent answers in this lab are scripted samples.

    Shared facts need an application step

    For Top Weights or a community T3 rule, one requester pays to obtain a ranking. The accepted answer stores a canonical list hash for the rule. Another included wallet can reuse that result without paying for another oracle question.

    An included wallet still calls applySharedFact(id, list) with the exact accepted list. The Registry checks the hash and membership, then records the fact for that caller. This application costs gas, but no additional oracle fee. A list being stored does not automatically make every member’s hasTrait true. Shared result and application.

    The list must be recovered as evidence, not invented from a similar ranking. The frontend can retrieve the completion payload and verify its hash against sharedFact. If that evidence is unavailable, membership is unknown. It is incorrect to label an empty failed retrieval as “not in the list.” The revised mock includes this recovery path and an explicit retry. Completion and exact-list verification.

    Mint Rule: define a reusable Community Fact

    Use Mint Rule when the built-in catalog does not express your condition. Choose one of five supported templates, fill the structured fields, inspect the composed question, then register the definition. The contract validates its grammar before charging the 6.4 IMD registration fee. Registration creates a rule ID; a wallet must separately verify that rule through Mint Facts.

    Rules are immutable. If you make a mistake, register a corrected definition with a new ID. The ID you see before submitting is not reserved: read the assigned ID from the confirmed result or SpecRegistered event. Community IDs run from 10001 through 65534. Different applications can consume the same ID without changing its definition. Registration and validation.

    Five concrete rule examples

    These are proposed definitions using real Ethereum contracts. They are not claims that a new rule has been registered or that a particular wallet already holds it. The count, sum and balance examples expand the earlier Sworn how-to material; the ranking and nonce examples complete the template set.

    TemplateConcrete definitionMeaning and limit
    T1 · Count eventsCurator Deposited events whose indexed contributor equals the claimant; threshold 3; blocks 25,769,870–25,789,604 inclusiveAt least three matching log entries. It does not deduplicate by transaction or identify a unique person.
    T2 · Sum eventsSame Curator event and claimant filter; sum amount; threshold 10000000000000000000 wei, or 10 ETH; same windowCumulative ETH sent through the game. Because deposits were refunded, this is neither unique capital nor current wealth.
    T3 · Rank a shared listCurator Deposited; group by indexed contributor; sum weightAdded; take the top 10 over the game windowA reusable top-10 ranking with descending sums and ascending-address tie breaks. One result, then a separate application per eligible wallet.
    T4 · Compare a historical viewCanonical Ethereum WETH, function balanceOf(address) view returns (uint256); value at least 1000000000000000000; window 26,256,800–26,264,000At least 1 WETH at the closing block only. It does not prove continuous ownership across the window.
    T5 · Historical nonceAccount nonce at least 20 at block 25,769,870; fromBlock = toBlock; no target contract or event textA historical nonce predicate. It is not an explorer transaction-count query or proof that the wallet has one human owner.

    The Curator target is 0xcB0b0531e86A9aC36Fa865cA8e3dbccF047FDA91. Canonical Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Copy the verified ABI’s complete signature into event fields rather than abbreviating Deposited as shown in this explanatory table. Curator source, WETH source, template semantics.

    Limits to check before registration

    T1–T4 require at least 7,200 inclusive blocks, with the closing block at least 64 blocks behind the validation height. T4 still needs this declared span even though it reads only the closing block. T5 requires one block at least 7,200 blocks old. These are block counts, not a promise of an exact elapsed day.

    Event rules require named parameters and an indexed address for the claimant or ranking key. T1/T2 permit one additional supported indexed filter. Summed fields must be unsigned integers. A T3 ranking contains 1–32 addresses. It cannot be replaced by an arbitrary unbounded leaderboard.

    The name is 1–32 supported ASCII characters; signatures follow a restricted grammar. Kind 6, the special Swarmed operator rule, is catalog-only. A valid grammar does not prove that archive data exists, that the oracle can finish the query, or that the predicate is useful. Check data availability and interpret the exact units before paying. Authoritative grammar and bounds.

    Read the card without confusing display with proof

    The contract Renderer produces SVG and metadata from Registry reads. Its thirteen hexagonal cells represent the catalog’s fixed families, with Swarmed in the center. Tiers and rare markers express built-in facts. Verifying a Community Fact does not create a new named hexagon.

    The first 39 accepted Community Facts add up to three rings per existing cell, in acceptance order. At 40 and beyond, the outer frame progresses in steps. Metadata lists the first 32 Community IDs and the total community count. That display limit is not a 32-fact credential limit: verifiedSpecsOf(wallet) returns the full community list, and hasTrait(wallet,id) checks an individual fact. Renderer and display limits.

    In the revised mock, click a family cell or a ring explanation to highlight the corresponding wallet facts. A cardless wallet has a preview too. This artwork illustrates the source-derived rules with synthetic data; its fills and frame path are not byte-identical deployed Renderer output.

    Even a real rendered image is not sufficient authentication. The Renderer can be called with another read adapter, and the SVG itself does not establish which Registry is authentic. Resolve the deployment and claimant, then query the predicate. An NFT marketplace owner field is not a substitute. Rendering trust boundary.

    Curate a list or consume a rule

    Decide whether your application needs a fixed list of addresses or a predicate checked when someone uses it. They are different policies.

    For a predicate such as Spawned 101 AND Uptime 701, query both facts on the authentic Registry. The user needs no card. For a fixed snapshot, first define the candidate universe, then evaluate every candidate at one pinned block, preserving chain, Registry, block number/hash, rule and unavailable reads with the export. An application can consume the resulting list separately from the live predicate. Consumer model.

    The original Curator census is one useful candidate source, not the complete universe of Sworn wallets. Starting only from NFT owners misses cardless users and can confuse purchasers with original claimants. An outside-census wallet may hold a valid community or operator fact. Discovering candidates and deciding eligibility are separate tasks.

    The revised mock’s Curator screen demonstrates this with eight known synthetic wallets, including no-card and outside-census examples. It supports direct and accepted facts, Community IDs, OR/AND, weights, ranges, CSV/JSON export and an address consumer check. Pending requests and stored-but-unapplied shared results do not qualify. Historical candidates are clearly separated from accepted records.

    Its Consume facts view also distinguishes current fact predicates from membership in the last exported list. An OR/AND hasTrait gate does not automatically enforce export weights, numeric ranges or exact saved membership. The mock is not a complete mainnet indexer, and its sample export is not an operational allowlist. See the builder documentation for the integration policy and evidence checklist.

    Fees, unsuccessful attempts and recovery

    Mint Card’s 0.1 IMD and Mint Rule’s 6.4 IMD are constants in this contract source; transaction gas is separate. New oracle requests pay the current Intake price and enforce the caller’s maximum. Applying a stored shared result costs gas only. Do not treat an old 0.5 IMD observation or the mock’s quote as a promise of today’s live price. Fee paths.

    False answers, disagreement, refusal and invalid delivery do not award the desired fact or refund the request price. A missing accepted record does not distinguish all these outcomes by itself; inspect request history. A wallet may retry a cleared unsuccessful attempt, but cannot request an already accepted fact again.

    If the Registry request is still pending, its Intake request is completed, and a valid true attestation was not delivered, settle may recover it before expiry. A callback that already cleared the request as false, invalid or failed cannot be repaired with settle; a cleared unsuccessful attempt requires a new paid request. A claimant can abandon a completed personal request immediately. Otherwise abandonment requires strictly more than 31 days after requesting; a shared pending request can then be abandoned by anyone. Abandoning clears the pending request, not its spent price. Recovery conditions.

    Mint and rule fees are forwarded to the BurnExecutor for bridging and burning on Base. Forwarding is the Registry’s action; bridge delivery and the eventual burn are later external steps. The Registry does not itself accept ETH, guarantee the destination burn, or offer the old sponsored/holder-claim paths. Current deployment limits.

    Know what you are trusting

    The Registry has no owner, pause or upgrade setter. That makes the published rules harder to change, but also removes an administrative repair path. A changed signer or incompatible upstream service can require a successor Registry. Existing accepted historical facts remain readable; new verification still depends on the external service.

    One fixed attester signs the result. Multiple panel seats do not prove independent humans, independent operators or independent data sources. Correct request binding prevents accepting the wrong signed question; it does not guarantee honest evidence collection. The oracle writer can delay delivery, and RPC/archive providers can make evidence unavailable. These are reasons to choose a policy proportional to the value at stake, not to infer trustlessness from an 11/7 badge. Sworn disclosure, IMD oracle trust model.

    Public wallet facts also expose relationships and behavior. A public blockchain record is not private merely because it omits a real name. The frontend, RPC and oracle infrastructure can observe queries and timing. Use only the evidence your policy needs; do not describe Sworn as a privacy-preserving identity system or a Sybil-proof personhood system.

    For the distinctive design choices and a balanced comparison with Merkle allowlists, ordinary NFT gating and attestation systems, continue with architecture and alternatives. For the current binding, exact interfaces and supporting sources, use the reference.
